facts.text: Helena Valley West Central lies 5 miles north of downtown Helena, within the Helena Micropolitan Statistical Area.
Before European settlement, the Helena Valley area served as a hunting and travel corridor for tribes like the Blackfeet, Salish, Crow, and Bannock.
After gold mining declined in the late 19th century, homesteading and agriculture expanded in Helena Valley, helped by the 1862 Homestead Act and the 1883 Northern Pacific Railroad.
Helena’s historic downtown, just a couple of miles from West Central, features Last Chance Road—a pedestrian mall lined with brick buildings that once housed Main Street.
The Montana Historical Society museum near West Central offers extensive exhibits on wildlife, Lewis and Clark, Native American culture, and paleontology.
